notes.l-qr-01: Kept as the set's easy direct wh-item (level 1, qr-wh), with a new scenario. 'Where's the orientation for the new interns being held?' -> B 'In the training room next to the cafeteria.' The key does not start with Yes. The distractors answer the wrong question type: A answers who with a similar-topic reply ('Mostly business students'), and C answers when ('It starts at nine thirty'). All four lines are new.
notes.l-qr-02: Now a statement with an indirect key. 'I can't open the quarterly sales spreadsheet on the shared drive.' -> C 'Martin was editing it a few minutes ago.' This implies the file is in use or locked. Both distractors are repeated-word traps: A reuses sales/quarter ('Sales were up again this quarter'), and B reuses drive in the sense of driving a car. Unit qr-wh -> qr-indirect, level 2 -> 3.
notes.l-qr-03: Now a choice question with an indirect key. 'Are you taking the train to the trade fair, or driving?' -> A 'Parking near the exhibition centre is really expensive.' This implies she will take the train. B reuses fair and answers when; C reuses train as a verb ('I've already trained the new staff'). Unit qr-wh -> qr-indirect, level 1 -> 3. Both voices are UK, so the text uses 'centre'.
notes.l-qr-04: Now a negative question: 'Haven't the new name badges come in yet?' -> C 'No, they should be here by Friday.' It is easy on purpose (level 1). The opening No is not a giveaway, because distractor A also opens with 'Yes' and reuses 'came in' ('Yes, I came in through the side door'). B reuses 'name'. Unit stays qr-yesno.
notes.l-qr-05: Still a tag question, but the key no longer starts with Yes: A 'That's right, I'll be the first speaker.' B uses 'present' as a noun (a repeated-word trap). C reports how the meeting went, though the meeting is tomorrow. It is easy on purpose (level 1). The response voice changed from bm_lewis to bm_george.
notes.l-qr-07: Content unchanged. Level 3 -> 2 to match the calibrated band (medium).
notes.l-qr-08: Content unchanged. Level 3 -> 2 to match the calibrated band (medium).
notes.l-conv-01: Added line 07 (M: at a client's office tomorrow, 'Could you leave mine on my chair?'). Questions: Q1 topic, unchanged. Q2 is new: what the moving company will do, from line 3, where 'furniture and computers' becomes 'Transport office equipment'. Q3 is new and hard: what the man asks. The listener must link 'mine' back to 'boxes and labels' in line 5, and the key is paraphrased as 'Set aside some packing materials for him'. Its lures are 'Visit a client with him' (same line), 'Postpone the packing deadline' and 'Pack up his personal items'. I dropped the old 'What will the woman do tomorrow?' because it overlapped the new last line. Level 1 -> 2.
notes.l-conv-02: Script unchanged (6 lines, so no new audio is needed). Added Q1 'Where does the man most likely work?' -> 'At a catering business', based on 'our platters' and the price per platter. Its lures are 'training center' (the woman's event) and 'courier company' (driver, deliveries). The problem and decision questions are kept as Q2 and Q3, with key positions moved to A and D. Q2 vocab changed so 'platter' is not repeated.
notes.l-conv-03: Q1 is now in the real quoted form: 'What does the woman imply when she says, "I've got a dentist appointment at three"?' -> D 'not free later in the afternoon' (evidence lines 0-1). I rewrote lines 04-06 and added 07 so that Tom's work is spread over two lines: 'Tom went over it [the back page]' and 'The page with all the prices?'. Q2 (hard) asks for this, paraphrased as 'Reviewed the cost information'. The photos / meeting room / printed copy lures come from other speakers or other lines. New Q3: the man's own action, where 'book a meeting room' becomes 'Reserve a room for their meeting'. Level stays 3.
notes.l-conv-04: Rewrote lines 02-06 and added 07. Q1 is new and hard: 'What does the woman mean when she says, "I'm not holding my breath"?' The context line is 'We were promised new laptops this spring, but ...', and the key is 'She doubts the new laptops will arrive as promised'. Its lures are a literal reading (not feeling well), a repeated 'hold' (on hold), and 'keep her old laptop'. Q2 (the man's offer this afternoon) is kept. Q3 (next action) is now truly the end of the conversation: 'On a silver sticker on the bottom' plus 'I'll turn it over' becomes 'Check the underside of her laptop'. Level 2 -> 3.
notes.l-talk-01: Lengthened to 6 lines and 118 words. The loosely motivated café line is gone. It is replaced by three new points: the main-entrance lifts will be very busy 8:30-9, so come in earlier; staff on the east side who can't manage the stairs can get a goods-lift pass from reception; and route maps will be posted by the staircases. Questions: Q1 topic, as before. Q2 asks why to come in earlier: 'those lifts' in line 3 must be linked to the main-entrance lifts in line 2, giving 'The remaining elevators will be crowded'. Q3 (hard) asks what some listeners can get from reception: 'a pass for the goods lift' becomes 'Access to a service elevator', with the map from line 5 as the lure.
notes.l-talk-02: Lengthened to 6 lines and 110 words. Line 3 now adds 'we've given you part of that time'. The parking part became 'the garage ... fills up early on forum days' followed by 'let me know by Wednesday and I'll send you a pass'. Questions: Q1 is new, 'Who most likely is Mr. Wei?' -> 'A guest speaker', with the organizer/technician/parking lures. Q2 (what change) is kept, with a new lure 'share his session with another speaker'. Q3 is new and hard: 'Why does the speaker mention the garage next to the venue?' -> 'To suggest that Mr. Wei reserve parking in advance' (lines 4-5). I dropped the old 'What does the speaker ask Mr. Wei to do?', because the parking line now contains a second request and that question would have two answers.
